episode_title: Here’s Why You Keep Saying Yes When You Want to Say No - Brainz Podcast with Jacqueline Young

real_qa.q: What is the Calm Authority Framework and how does it help leaders manage workplace stress and conflict?
real_qa.r: Calm Authority is a program Jacqueline offers when working with small groups or executives in high-stress management roles. It enables them to learn techniques to regulate their nervous system and respond to pressure and conflict from a grounded, parasympathetic state rather than a triggered sympathetic response.
real_qa.requete: Calm Authority Framework leadership stress management

real_qa.q: Why do capable, self-aware people understand their behavioral patterns but still struggle to change them?
real_qa.r: The reason patterns persist is because they are driven at the unconscious level. Jacqueline explains that the unconscious mind learned protective mechanisms in childhood—like freezing or fawning—and buried them deep. When triggered, these responses emerge automatically without conscious thought, which is why thinking alone cannot change them; work must happen at the unconscious level.
real_qa.requete: why can't change behavioral patterns understand but struggle

real_qa.q: What somatic and neurological responses did Jacqueline Young experience when facing a toxic work environment that mirrored childhood trauma?
real_qa.r: Walking into board meetings in a toxic workplace, Jacqueline found herself hyperventilating, unable to catch breath, palms sweating, and gut distressed—the exact same physical responses she had learned as a child living with an alcoholic father. She realized she was reverting to freeze or fawn responses, even though consciously she understood strategy, because the somatic conditioning was too deeply embedded.
real_qa.requete: somatic response trauma workplace freeze fawn

real_qa.q: What quick grounding technique does Jacqueline Young recommend to regulate the nervous system when triggered?
real_qa.r: Jacqueline recommends taking a deep breath through the nose, holding it, then exhaling through the mouth as if breathing through a straw to expel all air from the gut. This engages the vagus nerve via the diaphragm, automatically shifting the body from sympathetic to parasympathetic system, creating calm. Repeating this two or three times provides immediate regulation.
real_qa.requete: vagus nerve breathing exercise calm regulation technique

real_qa.q: Why does midlife become a critical turning point for women and men to reassess their life choices and purpose?
real_qa.r: Midlife is when people can look both backward and forward simultaneously. For the first time, especially for women, hormonal shifts reduce the biological drive to be caregivers, changing how the brain processes priorities. Simultaneously, when children reach around age 15, parenting demands shift, allowing parents to raise their head and ask fundamental questions about purpose, satisfaction, and what remains beyond work.
real_qa.requete: midlife turning point reassess purpose women hormones

guest.bio_context: Jacqueline D. Young brings more than 35 years of experience across education, executive leadership, counseling and human development. She is the creator of the Mindshift Leadership Method and the Calm Authority Framework, and author of the forthcoming book Fierce. Her career included a successful role in education until she spent over two years in a toxic work environment that prompted her deep exploration into neuroscience, neuropsychology, and the unconscious mind.
